statement: A decision problem is not its optimization, queueing or simulation encoding; lowering must declare exclusions and loss.
Hard, soft and chance constraints have different satisfaction and authority semantics.
A relaxation or repair proposal cannot change policy without an external relaxation authority.
An objective expression, achieved value, preference order and utility judgment are distinct.
A feasible point is not an optimal point and a locally solved result is not global optimality.
A primal incumbent and an objective bound constrain different sides of the unknown optimum.
Why execution stopped, whether a result exists, and the primal/dual status of each result are independent coordinates.
A solver status or feasibility claim is not an independently checked solution or certificate.
A time, memory, node, iteration or custom limit cannot be reported as proven infeasibility.
Infeasible, unbounded, infeasible-or-unbounded, no-result and unknown outcomes must remain distinct.
An IIS or conflict is neither necessarily unique nor a causal explanation of the world problem.
A heuristic best-known solution or search exhaustion under a budget is not an optimality proof.
A seed or stream identifier cannot reproduce a run without model, code, configuration, generator, allocation, schedule and environment identity.
Distinct random-stream identifiers do not by themselves prove statistical independence.
Observed arrivals, departures and occupancy do not uniquely determine queue classes, disciplines, service processes or routing.
Agreement with L=λW is a scoped conservation check, not proof of stationarity, stability or complete model validity.
High utilization is not by itself a bottleneck diagnosis or causal root cause.
A stable queue can still violate latency, loss, fairness or service-level objectives.
A simulation model and execution are representations of an intended use, not the real system or future truth.
Correct implementation of a conceptual model is distinct from evidence that the model is adequate for its intended use.
Repeated runs with different random streams are not independent implementations of the model or engine.
Warm-up deletion, termination horizon, censoring and initial-state policies must be explicit and cannot be silently inferred.
A simulation or optimization scenario difference is not an identified causal effect in the world.
A provider name or broad solver class does not satisfy an exact feature, numeric, certificate, target and resource requirement.
A checked proof log establishes only the admitted instance, rules, checker and certificate completeness.
An optimal, validated or simulated result remains a finding until an external decision authority accepts and acts on it.
